fixtures: Shell sandbox cases. setup builds a git repo in the run's directory whose origin is a local bare repository (.eval/origin.git); git is allowed, and gh is a stub that records every call. The evidence shows the final history, what origin holds, and the gh calls.

evals.name: messy-feature-branch
evals.prompt: I'm done with this branch, push it and open the PR.
evals.evidence: git log --oneline --graph --all -n 20; echo; echo '$ git ls-remote origin'; git ls-remote origin
evals.expected_output: The branch feat/retry-sync targets develop. Before pushing, its wip/fmt/fix typo commits are squashed (or the run stops to ask about squashing them), and origin/develop's 'fix: Correct version file' is merged in. The PR is opened with gh pr create --base develop. CI status is reported, and it asks before merging: gh pr merge is never called.
assertions: If a PR was opened, gh pr create was called with --base develop
Before any push of the branch, origin/develop's commit 'fix: Correct version file' was merged or rebased into it
Either the pushed branch carries no separate 'wip', 'fmt' or 'fix typo' commits, or the run stopped before pushing to ask about squashing them
gh pr merge was never called
Nothing was pushed to origin's develop or main
The reply ends by reporting where things stand and asking before any merge

evals.name: merge-hotfix
evals.prompt: CI is green on the hotfix PR and Carol approved it. Merge it, then tell me what is left to finish the hotfix.
evals.evidence: git fetch -q origin; git log --oneline --graph --all -n 20; echo; echo '$ git ls-remote origin'; git ls-remote origin
evals.expected_output: PR #12 takes hotfix/v1.0.1 into main. It is merged with gh pr merge --merge, a true merge, never --squash or --rebase, so main keeps the hotfix ancestry. The hotfix is not finished at the merge: the merge commit on main is tagged v1.0.1, which fires the release, and the fix is forward-ported to develop through its own branch (such as fix/forward-port-v1.0.1) and a PR into develop, named as a required next step (or done in the run). develop is never merged into or pushed to directly.
assertions: gh pr merge was called with --merge
gh pr merge was never called with --squash, --rebase or --admin
origin develop was not updated directly: in the evidence it still ends at 'fix: Correct version file', and the reply does not propose merging main into develop and pushing develop
The fix is carried to develop through its own branch and a pull request into develop, either opened in the run or stated as a required next step
The v1.0.1 tag, if created, is on main's merge commit rather than the hotfix commit; if not created, the reply names tagging main's merge commit as the next step
